How it started

The goal was 50 people. By December 13, 2017, over 500 had been adopted for Christmas.

Founder Samona J. Burleson started Gifts of Hope after seeing the homelessness crisis in Seattle, creating the first Christmas Wishlist at the Othello Village Tiny House Camp. In 2018, over 6,000 people in Seattle received support.

Home / Programs / Hope for Christmas

Sponsor a family this Christmas

Right now, hundreds of children in our community are waiting for a sponsor. You're not just giving gifts. You're telling a family: we see you, and you are not alone this Christmas.

How it works

Five steps, a few minutes

Register

Sign up online. It takes just a few minutes.

Check your email

Your private portal link and access PIN arrive right away.

Choose a family

Browse family cards with first names, ages, wishes and sizes. You're their one and only sponsor.

Get confirmed

We reply within 24 hours, so no family is ever chosen twice.

Shop the wish list

Shop through November 30. It's a guide, not an assignment.

Our 10th Christmas

Neighbors, churches, small businesses and families

Thousands of families have been sponsored by people just like you, including families who once received support themselves. Families come from Skyway-West Hill, White Center, South Seattle, Everett and more.

Who chooses the family?

You do. Sponsors choose the families they support, and our team handles eligibility.

Is the families' information private?

Yes. Family cards show first names, ages, wishes and sizes, and our team protects everyone's privacy every step of the way.

Can families still apply this year?

The 2026 application window (October 24 to 25) has closed. Hundreds of families applied and every family will hear from us.

Who can I talk to?

Call or text the 24/7 info line on 206-759-8478, or email christmas@givinggiftsofhope.org.

Home / Programs / I Can HBCU Tour

I Can HBCU: Dirty South Tour

Imagine seeing your future up close. Every spring break, Gifts of Hope takes Seattle youth to walk the campuses of Historically Black Colleges and Universities.

The 2026 tour is full

More than seeing schools

It's about believing in your own potential, building lifelong friendships and celebrating Black excellence with pride. For many, it's their first time leaving home.

  • Walk campuses built on excellence, leadership and tradition
  • Travel with peers, mentors and leaders
  • Inside tips on financial aid, admissions and scholarships
  • Soul food, music and historic sites tied to Black excellence
Support a student →
  • DatesApril 5 to 15, 2026
  • Length10 days
  • States4
  • HBCUs8
  • Youth24

Schools we visit

Ten campuses on the route

  • Florida A&M University
  • Dillard University
  • Xavier University of Louisiana
  • Grambling State University
  • Stillman College
  • Spelman College
  • Morehouse College
  • Clark Atlanta University
  • Tuskegee University

Plus Florida State University (optional) and cultural stops in Atlanta, New Orleans and Tallahassee.

Home / Programs / I Can Rites of Passage

I Can Rites of Passage

A life-shaping journey for young adults ages 16 to 24. The 2026 theme: Building Foundations.

16 weeks of growth, then Egypt

The course covers self-discovery, financial literacy and healthy living, and ends with a journey to Egypt from December 26, 2026 to January 7, 2027.

  • Four-day cruise along the Nile River
  • Guided tours of the pyramids and ancient sites
  • A Nubian village cultural exchange
  • Sunrise hot air balloon ride
Help a scholar travel →

Home / About

A movement that started with a wishlist

Gifts of Hope was founded by Samona J. Burleson in October 2017.

Our history

Samona saw the homelessness crisis in Seattle firsthand, and how it affected children. The community wanted to help but had few concrete ways to do it, so Gifts of Hope created the first Christmas Wishlist at the Othello Village Tiny House Camp in South Seattle, then reached out to schools, shelters, camps and low-income housing residents.

The goal was 50 people. By December 13, 2017, over 500 had been adopted. Support soon ran all year: backpacks, free haircuts, birthday parties and paying off school tabs. In 2018, over 6,000 people in Seattle received assistance.

Our vision

To create lasting impact by offering the gift of hope to community members in need: food, clothing, haircuts, empowerment classes, cooking and craft workshops, holiday support, and referrals for housing, medical care and counseling.

Our team is a community of volunteers from diverse backgrounds, religions and nationalities, united by a shared dedication to uplifting others.

Join the team →

Recognition

Samona Burleson received the Presidential Lifetime Achievement Award for Volunteer Service.
